markets.rules_primary: If the 15-minute time-weighted average of the Kalshi American Power Index - Midterms (KPOW Midterms) ending at 11:00 AM EST on November 3, 2026 is above -22.6, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The average is calculated and published by Pyth under the methodology in Appendix B of the KPOW Midterms filing and is used at the precision Pyth publishes it, without rounding. The target is the average ending at 10:00 AM EST, rounded to the nearest 0.1. Only trades at or before 11:00 AM EST count, and a price move held by the index's price check counts only once it is accepted.

The index runs from -50, Democratic candidates certain to win every weighted race, to +50, Republican candidates certain to win every weighted race, so a higher average is more Republican.

The following do NOT count:
Any single published value of the index, including the 30-second updates and the value at 11:00 AM EST
Charts, indicative figures and third-party recalculations

A constituent market that stops trading, is determined or settles keeps its last accepted price, so a race being called or certified does NOT, by itself, move the index.

For a 1:00pm ET observation, use the 12:59pm candle, covering 12:59:00pm up to but excluding 1:00:00pm ET. No averaging applies. The closing Pyth yield, expressed as a percentage, is rounded to five decimal places using round-half-up before comparison with the strike.

Other sources and stale or carried-forward values cannot substitute. If reliable data is unavailable by expiration, or none is expected, settlement is at the Exchange-determined last fair price, unless a "No data" strike is listed. Corrections, expiration and Rule 7.1 review follow the full contract rules. Kalshi is not affiliated with Pyth.
